title: I Read 10 Books in October and Ranked Them All
creator: Hana Sato
description:
October reading wrap up! Ten books, one spooky, two that made me cry on the train.

Thank you to Room to Read for sponsoring today's video! Help a girl stay in school: https://www.roomtoread.org/hana

Books mentioned:
The Thursday Murder Club - Richard Osman
Piranesi - Susanna Clarke
Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow - Gabrielle Zevin
The Remains of the Day - Kazuo Ishiguro
Demon Copperhead - Barbara Kingsolver

Goodreads: hanareadsalot

sentences.t: Hi friends, it is wrap up time, and October was a weirdly good reading month for me.
I read ten books, which for me is a lot, and I'm going to rank every single one from my least favorite to my favorite.
There are a couple of hot takes in here, so, please be nice in the comments.
Before I start, today's video is brought to you by Room to Read.
If you haven't heard of them, Room to Read is a nonprofit that works on literacy and girls' education in places like Nepal, Tanzania and Cambodia.
They train teachers, they print children's books in local languages, and they run a program that helps girls actually finish secondary school.
And as someone who basically made her whole personality out of library books as a kid, this one really means a lot to me.
So far they've reached more than forty million children, which, I had to read that number twice.
If you'd like to support a girl through a full year of school, you can donate at roomtoread dot org slash hana.
The link is the first thing in the description, and anything you give, even five dollars, goes a really long way.
Thank you so much to Room to Read for sponsoring this video.
Okay, number ten, my least favorite of the month.
This was a thriller I picked up at the airport and I genuinely don't remember the main character's name.
That's all I'm going to say about that.
Number nine and eight are both fine, perfectly fine books that I'll never think about again.
One was a romance where the whole conflict could have been solved with a single phone call.
Number seven is The Thursday Murder Club.
I know everyone loves this one, and it is cozy and funny, but I found the mystery itself kind of thin.
Great characters though, I'd absolutely have tea with every one of them.
Number six is The Remains of the Day, which was a reread.
It's so quiet and so sad, and I think I appreciated it more at thirty than I did at nineteen.
Numbers five and four I'm grouping together because they're both literary fiction about families falling apart, and I read them back to back, which was a mistake.
Okay, top three.
Number three is Demon Copperhead.
It is long, it is heavy, and the first hundred pages are rough, but the voice is just incredible.
I cried on the train, a man offered me a tissue, it was a whole thing.
Number two is Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow.
It's about two friends who make video games together over thirty years, and I didn't think I cared about video games, and it turns out I care a lot.
There's one chapter in the middle that I won't spoil, but if you've read it, you know.
And my number one book of October is Piranesi.
I went in completely blind, which I'd really recommend.
It's short, it's strange, and it's the most peaceful book I've ever read, even though some genuinely awful things happen in it.
I finished it and immediately started it again, which I never do.
So that's my October.
Tell me your favorite read of the month down below, because my November list is very empty right now.
Bye friends, happy reading.
